chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah from Muhammad ibn Muslim and others from both of them, both said:

Regarding the dog, when a man sends it and calls out (the name of God), they said: If it catches it and you find its throat still fresh (alive), then slaughter it; and if you find it has already killed it and eaten from it, then eat what remains.

key_terms.وَيُسَمِّي: and he calls out (the name of God)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating meat from game caught by a hunting dog that has already eaten some of it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the condition of 'adhrā' (slaughter) for game caught by a trained dog, emphasizing that the animal must be slaughtered if still alive to be considered halal. It further establishes that if the dog has already killed and consumed part of the prey, the remaining meat is permissible, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the dog's bite constitutes a valid slaughter provided the animal was alive at the moment of the bite. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the permissibility of wild game hunted by dogs.
